clue.text: Precious stone displayed in Warwickshire town (not the centre)

indicators.note: without its centre, the middle letter of the town's name is thrown out

parts.note: Rugby is a market town in Warwickshire, birthplace of the sport

explanation.surface: A gem is put on show in a Midlands town.
explanation.walkthrough: RUGBY has five letters, so its centre is the G; drop it and RUBY remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruby is a red gemstone, one example of a precious stone.

clue.text: Artist's club in Moroccan capital

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword artist
a bat is a club used to strike a ball

explanation.surface: An artist belongs to a club in Morocco's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe s reads as 'has', joining the artist to the club.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabat is the seat of government of Morocco, its capital city.

clue.text: Anger about British band in area of Protestant fundamentalism

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for anger wraps round the letter for British

parts.note: bile is bitter anger or ill temper
B is the abbreviation for British
a belt is a band worn round the waist

explanation.surface: Fury erupts over a British music group in a region of strict Protestants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests musicians, but it is a strip of material. The Bible Belt is the southern and midwestern USA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible Belt names the American region where evangelical Protestant fundamentalism is culturally dominant.

clue.text: Red dye boy detected in body of water in central Africa

definitions.text: body of water in central Africa

parts.note: lake is a crimson pigment or dye
a boy's name

explanation.surface: A red dye from a boy is spotted in an African lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Lake as a pigment is an old painter's term for a deep red colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Edward lies on the border of Uganda and the Congo, a lake in central Africa.

clue.text: Article on a composer reportedly produced by psychiatrist

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
taken as written

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the composer's name is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: Franz Liszt, the Hungarian composer, pronounced list

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about a composer is written up by a psychiatrist.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places the first part above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An analyst is a psychoanalyst, a common informal term for a psychiatrist or therapist.

clue.text: Aged men playing closing moves on chessboard

indicators.note: the men are at play, moving about, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Elderly men at a chess table make their final moves.
explanation.definitionFit: The endgame is the last phase of a chess match, when few pieces are left on the board.

clue.text: The way in which our PM may make a public statement?

definitions.text: The way in which our PM may make a public statement?

parts.words: The way in which our PM may make a public statement?
parts.note: surface reading: the manner in which the Prime Minister addresses the nation; setter's reading: way means a road, the London road where the PM lives and speaks to the press outside the front door

explanation.walkthrough: 'Way' looks like 'manner' but means a street; British prime ministers make statements at a lectern outside Number 10.
explanation.definitionFit: Downing Street in London holds the Prime Minister's official residence, and its doorstep is where announcements are made.

clue.text: A western wood, flooded

parts.note: taken as written
W is the abbreviation for western
ash is a kind of timber

explanation.surface: A forest in the west lies under floodwater.
explanation.definitionFit: Awash means covered with water, swamped, the state of a flooded place.

clue.text: Disguised in frock, dupe cast?

indicators.note: something cast is thrown or moulded anew, so the letters are thrown into a fresh order

parts.note: a frock is a dress
the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone in a frock may have been fooled into playing a part.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressed up can mean disguised by costume, or made to look like something else.

clue.text: Tiny tot by magnificent piano

parts.note: a baby is a tiny tot
grand means splendid, magnificent

explanation.surface: A toddler sits beside a splendid piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby grand is a small grand piano, one particular type of the instrument.

clue.text: Middle of night TV also dreary? Possibly, when the number watching is at its lowest

definitions.text: when the number watching is at its lowest

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the letters may be reordered
the middle of a word is its central letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: the central letter of a five-letter word
the letters to be rearranged with the one before

explanation.surface: Late-night television is dull, which is perhaps why few people watch it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as a description of the answer, so the wordplay and definition run together.
explanation.definitionFit: The graveyard slot is broadcasting jargon for the late-night period with the smallest audience.

clue.text: First sign of whopper, robust creature

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: the opening letter
hale means healthy and robust

explanation.surface: The first hint of something huge: a sturdy beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A whale is a sea mammal, an example of a creature, and suitably a whopper.

clue.text: Old film mag ceases to be

parts.note: The Lady is a long-running British weekly women's magazine
to vanish is to disappear, cease to exist

explanation.surface: An old magazine goes out of print.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lady is a British magazine founded in 1885, known for its classified ads for nannies and housekeepers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lady Vanishes is Alfred Hitchcock's 1938 thriller, a classic old movie.

clue.text: Introduce and compere tense show

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to host a programme and bring on its guests
second meaning: the grammatical tense for the here and now
third meaning: to display or exhibit

explanation.surface: Host a nervous television show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' reads as nervous, describing the show, but it is the grammar term.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to host or display, and as a noun it names the grammatical tense of current action.

clue.text: Condemn professional writer

parts.note: pro is short for professional
a scribe is a writer

explanation.surface: Criticise a writer who does it for a living.
explanation.definitionFit: To proscribe is to forbid or denounce, so it means to condemn something officially.

clue.text: Duff gen put down leaving country

indicators.note: duff is British slang for faulty or useless, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: gen, slang for information, rearranged
to land is to put an aircraft down

explanation.surface: Bad information has been set down as someone leaves the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaving' looks like departure but just means 'resulting in'.
explanation.definitionFit: England is one of the nations making up the United Kingdom, a country.

clue.text: A teal viciously biting another aquatic bird every second

indicators.note: biting means holding between the jaws, so one part goes inside the other
a vicious attack throws things into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A duck savagely attacks another water bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Alternate as an adjective describes things happening every other time, one in two.

clue.text: Away from port, unconscious, hospital room required

parts.note: knocked out means unconscious
a ward is a hospital room

explanation.surface: Away from the harbour, someone passes out and needs a hospital bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Outward bound is the nautical phrase for a ship heading away from its home harbour.

clue.text: After party, bet with elderly lady of means

indicators.note: after places the second word below the first in this down entry

parts.note: a do is a party
a wager is a bet

explanation.surface: After a party, a rich old woman places a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager is a widow holding a title or property from her late husband, typically a wealthy older woman.

clue.text: What driver may need in Jeep? It's to pass!

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the words that follow, running across them

parts.note: the run of letters from the end of the first word to the start of the last

explanation.surface: A driver stuck behind a Jeep wonders whether to overtake.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit stop is a racing car's pause for fuel and tyres, which a racing driver needs.

clue.text: Obvious about one, one receiving medical treatment

indicators.note: about means round the outside, so the word for obvious wraps the numeral

parts.note: patent means plain or obvious
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: It's clear that someone is being treated by a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient is a person under the care of a doctor or in hospital.

clue.text: Appear sensible, stop fantasising

parts.note: to come is to appear
down to earth means practical and sensible

explanation.surface: Seem level-headed and quit daydreaming.
explanation.definitionFit: To come down to earth is an idiom for returning to reality after dreams or euphoria.

clue.text: Pole finally needed to support damaged palm tree

indicators.note: damaged things are knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
in a down entry the supporting piece sits underneath the rest

parts.note: the letters rearranged
E, east, is one of the compass poles in crosswords

explanation.surface: A pole props up a damaged palm tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Palm tree' looks like the definition; palm is the fodder and tree alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The maple is a deciduous tree, the source of syrup and the leaf on Canada's flag.

clue.text: Wedges demonstrated by male, champion golfer

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
Ernie Els, South African major-winning golfer

explanation.surface: A man and a top golfer show off their wedges, the golf clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Wedges are golf clubs in the surface, but here they are wedge-shaped shoe heels.
explanation.definitionFit: Wedges are shoes with a solid sloping sole, a kind of raised heel.

clue.text: Urge one politician to face the Spanish

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP, Member of Parliament
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Press a politician to confront the Spanish.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or push someone forward, much as to urge them.

clue.text: Dog in tea garden, barking

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters go crazy and are reordered

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dog is barking in a café garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' looks like what the dog does, but as 'barking mad' it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Dane is a very large breed of dog.

clue.text: Choose to address all the voters

parts.note: to elect is to choose by vote
to orate is to make a speech

explanation.surface: Decide to give a speech to every voter.
explanation.definitionFit: The electorate is the whole body of people entitled to vote in an election.

clue.text: Steamship on north-eastern Loch

indicators.note: on means placed after in an across entry, so the ship follows the direction

parts.note: NE is the abbreviation for north-eastern
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A steamer sails on a loch in the north-east of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Loch Ness is the Scottish lake famous for its legendary monster, known simply by its name.
